name: Tarifit (Riffian Berber)

ancestors.notes: Zenati Northern Berber; Tarifit is the principal Berber variety of the Rif (northern Morocco).
Spanish adstrate from the Spanish protectorate era and ongoing contact through the Spanish exclaves of Melilla and Ceuta on the Rif coast (Wikipedia, Tarifit: loanwords such as familiya 'family').

Arabic adstrate (Moroccan Darija and Classical/religious Arabic): Wikipedia (Tarifit, citing Kossmann & Mourigh 2020) estimates ~51.7% of Tarifit vocabulary (56.1% of nouns, 44.1% of verbs) is borrowed, chiefly from Arabic, plus Spanish and French.

notes: Tarifit / Riffian Berber, a Zenati Northern Berber language of the Rif region of northern Morocco (~1.2M speakers). Modelled here in the Berber Latin alphabet (the same convention family as kab.json/shy.json), the dominant script online and in most publications per Wikipedia; Tifinagh (official in Morocco since 2003) and Arabic script are also in use and not modelled here. VOWELS: a basic system of /i, u, a/ plus a lax central /ə/ (written e in the Latin convention, as in Kabyle/Shawiya); /i a u/ have lax allophones [ɪ æ ʊ] and, near pharyngealised consonants, pharyngealised allophones [ɪˤ ɑˤ ʊˤ] (not modelled as separate graphemes — this is allophony, not orthography). CONSONANTS follow Kossmann & Mourigh (2020) 'An introduction to Tarifiyt Berber (Nador, Morocco)' as summarised by Wikipedia: nasals /m n ŋ/; plosives with pharyngealised counterparts /p pˤ t tˤ tʃ k kːʷ q ʔ b d dˤ dʒ g gːʷ/; fricatives /f θ s sˤ ʃ ʃˤ ç x ħ β ð ðˤ z zˤ ʒ ɣ ʕ ɦ/; approximants /l lˤ j w/; flaps/trills /ɾ ɾˤ r rˤ/; most consonants have geminate counterparts except /ŋ, tʃ, ʔ/. The most distinctive Riffian feature relative to other Northern Berber varieties (Kabyle, Shawiya) is the correspondence of other dialects' /l/ to Riffian /r/ (traditionally written ř), and an r-vocalisation process producing diphthong-like sequences ([ɛa], [a~æ], [ɔa]) — not modelled here for lack of a specific orthographic convention sourced this session, so ř is mapped to plain /r/ pending that. Only the plain (non-pharyngealised) consonant series is populated in graphemes for now; the pharyngealised series and the emphatic/gemination alternations documented by Kossmann & Mourigh would need their own cited orthographic convention (dot-under letters, as in shy.json) before being added — left for a follow-up pass rather than guessed. Massive Arabic/Spanish/French lexical borrowing (Kossmann & Mourigh 2020, cited via Wikipedia) is recorded as adstrate ancestry, not as extra graphemes.
